tasks.short: Explain the procedure, check safety questions, position and reassure the patient and observe them during the scan.

steps.what: Radiographer explains procedures to the patient
Patient answers safety questions on contrast allergy, pregnancy and implants: at the scanner today, in the portal before the visit after the change
Radiographer asks about contrast allergy, pregnancy and implants
Radiographer positions and reassures the patient
Radiographer observes patients to ensure safety and comfort during the scan

tasks.design: Patients fill in the safety questionnaire (contrast allergy, kidney function, pregnancy, implants) in the patient portal ({OTHER}) before the visit, and the radiographer reviews the answers and confirms the critical ones in person. Explaining, positioning and observing stay with the radiographer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every safety question was asked from scratch at the scanner.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient portals collect questionnaires into the record before the visit.
tasks.still_hard: Answers given at home can be wrong; critical items must be confirmed.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a claustrophobic patient so the scan can go ahead.

evidence.claim: Patient portals collect questionnaires into the record before a visit.
Using ionising radiation is a reserved act; others act on assignment with instructions.

assumptions: Boundary: from the scheduled exam to the completed scan; reporting is outside.
Input contract: questionnaire filled in by the patient in the portal; questions set by the radiology department; fallback is asking at the scanner.
Explaining, positioning and observing do not change.
Patients' time is priced as customer time, not as the radiographer's savings.
unknowns: Share of patients who fill in the questionnaire.
research_questions: Does time at the scanner per patient fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients fill the questionnaire before the visit, so most questions are asked at the scanner (s2 keeps 90) (1.6); high: most patients use the portal (5.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter exam details, note incidents, complete the exam and send images, write technical notes and compile dose statistics.

steps.what: Radiographer types dose, contrast and technique into the radiology system
Radiographer records incidents and deviations
Radiographer checks the exam before completing it: patient, series and images against the request
Radiographer completes the checked exam, which sends its images to the archive
Radiographer writes technical notes for the radiologist
Radiographer prepares monthly dose and exam reports: in a spreadsheet today; after the change reads the dose dashboard and notes what stands out

tasks.design: Scanners send dose and technique data as structured reports to the radiology system ({OTHER}) and the dose register; the radiographer only scans the contrast batch barcode. The radiographer checks the exam and completes it once, which sends its images to the archive; technical notes are written as today, and a dose dashboard replaces the monthly spreadsheet. Incident reports stay a person's account on the existing form.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dose and technique were retyped, and statistics compiled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Scanners export dose and technique data that radiology systems and dose registers read.
tasks.still_hard: Older scanners do not send structured dose data.
tasks.human_edge: Writing the one technical note that explains an odd image.

reach.learn: Whether a dose dashboard finds outliers sooner.

evidence.claim: Scanners send dose and technique data as structured reports to radiology systems and dose registers.
The medical dossier is kept 20 years and patients may ask who viewed it.
Logs of radiographers' work can count as staff monitoring, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the completed scan to reports; the radiologist's report is outside.
Input contract: dose data from the scanners; pick lists set by the senior radiographer; fallback is typing.

Incident reports and technical notes stay a person's account and keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 for scanning the contrast batch and checking the data; s4 keeps 10 for completing the exam; s6 keeps 15 for reading the dashboard each month.
Dashboards show dose per exam type, not per radiographer.
research_questions: Do dose outliers get noticed sooner?

incremental.description: Radiographer checks dose data when the export fails.

approvals.approved_version: The images and series of this exam exactly as checked by the radiographer in s3, sent once to the image archive on completing the exam; added images need a new check and completion.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older scanners without structured dose reports keep typing (s1 keeps 70) and the dashboard needs monthly clean-up (s6 keeps 40) (29.0); high: all scanners send structured reports (46.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check each image for diagnostic quality, decide on retakes, log rejects with reasons, review reject rates and discuss quality with radiologists.

steps.what: Radiographer reviews computer-generated images to determine if they are satisfactory for diagnostic purposes
Radiographer decides whether a retake is needed
Radiographer logs rejected images and reasons: on paper today, at the console with a reason from a pick list after the change
Radiographer reviews monthly repeat rates: counted in a spreadsheet today, read from the reject dashboard after the change
Radiographer discusses image quality with radiologists

tasks.design: Rejected images are logged at the console with a reason from a pick list ({OTHER}), and a reject-analysis dashboard shows rates per exam type and reason each month. Judging image quality, deciding retakes and discussing quality with radiologists stay with the radiographer; rates are shown per exam type, not per person.
tasks.previous_blocker: The console's reject logging was not set up with reason codes, so rejects were noted on paper and counted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Imaging consoles can log rejected images with a reason from a pick list once it is configured.
tasks.still_hard: Whether an image is good enough is clinical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a slight rotation will hide the fracture line.

evidence.claim: Imaging systems log rejected images with reasons for reject analysis.
Reject logs per radiographer can count as staff monitoring, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from acquired images to quality actions; the radiologist's reading is outside.
Input contract: reject reasons set by the quality radiographer; fallback is paper logs.
Judging, deciding and logging each reject keep their full time; picking a reason instead of writing it is not a saving. s4 keeps 15 for reading the dashboard each month.
No AI judges image quality in this design.

incremental.description: No new work: picking the reason is the log in s3, and the quality radiographer keeps the reasons list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the console export needs manual clean-up each month (s4 keeps 60) (4.0); high: the dashboard runs by itself (8.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the request, choose the protocol from the department list, check prior exams, ask the physician about unclear requests and consult the radiologist.

steps.what: Radiographer determines patients' x-ray needs by reading requests from physicians
Radiographer looks up prior exams and implants in the record
Radiographer phones the requesting physician about unclear requests
Radiographer chooses the protocol from the department list

loop.input: The request text, the clinical question, prior exams and implants, any clarification from the physician, and the department's fixed protocol list.
loop.output: One protocol from the list with the request phrase it rests on.
loop.check: Code accepts only protocol codes on the department list. A second check compares the quoted request phrase with the protocol's indication and flags proposals the phrase does not support; the radiographer reads the request and confirms every protocol, and unclear requests go to the radiologist.
loop.stop: One proposal per request; no confident match means the radiographer chooses.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests are free text; keyword rules miss clinical questions.

steps.what: Radiographer asks the radiologist when the protocol is in doubt
Radiographer checks the final protocol against the request, priors and any advice, and the scanner it goes to
Radiographer releases the checked protocol to the scanner worklist

tasks.design: Prior exams and implant records are shown with the request in the radiology system ({OTHER}). After the radiographer has read priors and any physician clarification, a bounded step proposes a protocol from the department's fixed list, quoting the request phrase it rests on. The radiographer confirms the final protocol, with the radiologist when in doubt, and only the confirmed protocol goes to the scanner worklist. Reading requests, phoning physicians and consulting the radiologist stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protocols were chosen by reading each request and searching the list.
tasks.enabler_now: A study found language models choosing from fixed protocol lists rarely chose unacceptably.
tasks.still_hard: Accuracy dropped at another hospital; local validation is needed before use.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that the clinical question does not match the exam requested.
tasks.altitude: The radiographer confirms proposed protocols instead of choosing from scratch.

evidence.claim: Choosing MRI protocols from fixed lists, a language model's choices were unacceptable in under 1% of cases; freely composed protocols were accepted 76.5% in-house and 46.7% elsewhere.
Software with a medical purpose is a medical device.
AI in a device that needs notified body assessment is high-risk under the AI Act.

assumptions: Boundary: from the request to the confirmed protocol; scanning is outside.
Input contract: requests from physicians through order entry; protocol list kept by the radiologists; fallback is choosing by hand.
Phoning physicians and consulting radiologists do not change.
The step is validated locally before use.
No focal upkeep: the radiologists keep the protocol list and review a sample. s7 keeps 20 for the release.
unknowns: Whether the proposal tool needs device certification.
research_questions: How often does the radiographer change the proposal?

incremental.description: Radiologists review a sample of confirmed protocols.

approvals.approved_version: The protocol for this exam exactly as checked by the radiographer in s6, set once on the worklist of the scanner named there; a change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many requests are unclear and priors sit outside the system (s2 keeps 80, s4 keeps 85) (11.4); high: most requests match a standard protocol (25.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The radiographer keeps patients, image judgement and protocol confirmation; retyping, counting and searching shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A radiographer who spends saved minutes with anxious patients.
